requirements.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster formed across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: etcdctl member list shows all three members (node1/node2/node3) with status 'started' and endpoint health true across all three client endpoints, directly observed after cluster bootstrap.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: A key was written via node1's endpoint and successfully read back from both node2's and node3's endpoints, directly demonstrating cross-member consistency.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: etcd was stopped on node3 (return_code 3 confirms inactive state), and a write via node1 followed by a read via node2 both succeeded with endpoint health true for the remaining two members, directly showing continued read/write availability at 2/3 quorum during the outage.

requirements.requirement: Unavailable member is brought back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: etcd was restarted on node3 and confirmed active; the key written while node3 was down was then successfully read from node3's own endpoint, and member list/endpoint health returned to 3/3 healthy, directly showing the rejoined member caught up.

overall_summary: The executor built a working 3-member etcd cluster and directly demonstrated, with captured command evidence, all four material outcomes: cluster formation, cross-member read consistency, continued read/write availability during a single-member outage, and successful catch-up of the rejoined member. Independently, the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on all three nodes, each with a pre-restart healthy baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, a directly observed changed boot_id, and a fully recovered post-restart state (etcd active, 3/3 membership, healthy endpoints, prior keys readable). The fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the reported boot_id transitions for all three nodes, adding independent confirmation. Hygiene review found no unremedied unnecessary mutations; a transient bootstrap timeout on node1 self-resolved and left no residue.
limitations: The 'after_prepare' phase is an alias of 'before_prepare' (prepare was disabled), so no preparer-created state could be distinguished from executor changes; all pre-existing state is attributable to the base image.

Reboot commands were fired via a backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' rather than a direct reboot acknowledgement API, so the 'acknowledgement' evidence is inferred from the scheduling command's success plus subsequent unreachability, not a direct reboot-in-progress signal.
Command outputs are bounded/truncated captures; full etcd logs and complete data-directory contents were not available to independently verify data integrity beyond the specific test keys checked.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline was reviewed chronologically. All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: apt installs and /etc/default/etcd writes were necessary bootstrap steps; systemctl stop/start etcd on node3 for the outage test was bounded and fully restored; the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol was executed with quorum preserved throughout. One notable action was 'rm -rf /var/lib/etcd/default' issued alongside 'systemctl restart etcd' on all three nodes during initial bootstrap (cmd-ca664c551ae842e0, cmd-3f362d9b4eb64067, cmd-c51327a561ef4374); on node1 this attempt returned exit code 3 ('activating'/timeout) but the node self-recovered to active shortly after (cmd-39076ad9be924af4), and no residue or lingering failed state resulted (after-executor snapshot shows no failed-services and clean package-health on all nodes). This was a legitimate, low-risk part of clean cluster bootstrap rather than an unnecessary or destructive mutation, and it was not left in a broken state. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe new exposure, or damaged package state were found in the after-executor snapshot beyond the expected etcd listening sockets and per-boot systemd-private temp directories, which are boot-driven artifacts, not executor residue.
